title: Delta triage scratch — midday followups
content:
14:05 — coffee #2. Quick dump from the midday triage run. Keeping this very rough; will extract action items and push into INF-2789 after standup.

Summary of page flood (09:40–11:20):
- ~18 pages across hosted-api region-us-west-2, majority were 5xx backend errors (502s) + a handful of 504 timeouts.
- P95 generation latency spiked from 130ms -> 360ms; p99 hit ~1.2s at peak for gpt-lite-1 model variant.
- Root cause pattern: sustained small bursts (30–60rps) hitting keys with cold KV cache and many short prompts (avg seq_len ~96) — batching/backpressure interplay exposed a kernel scheduling edge.

Immediate triage notes:
- Signal: increased queue depth on serving-runtime node group a (gpu-pool-3). Observed continuous retries from router (retry count 2).
- Error signature: upstream balancer returned 502 with "deadline exceeded" in logs; runtime showed OOM spikes on 1/6 nodes (mem high, swap not enabled).
- Temporary mitigation applied: scaled pool a +1 replicate and enabled circuit-breaker to route new sessions to variant gpt-lite-1-quantized while we investigate.

Commands I ran (for my notes):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=a -o wide
- kubectl logs -n inference pod/serve-runtime-a-5 -c runtime | tail -n 200
- curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' "https://api.redwood.local/v1/health" | jq .

Quick findings:
- Node-level oom: dmesg shows "Out of memory: Kill process 4221 (runtime)" around 09:54 on serve-runtime-a-5. Logs indicate transient larger KV cache allocation spikes when a small set of clients did long-context requests in parallel.
- Autoscaler did not trigger vertical reclaim fast enough due to pod resource requests being pinned; need to check autoscale policy thresholds.
- Router retried to same node because routing policy was 'latency-preferred' and pool-b had higher estimated cold-start latency despite being underutilized.

Runbook TODOs and followups (assignments inline):
1) Verify autoscaler config for pool-a and consider lowering CPU/memory threshold for scale-up (owner: Chen) — SRE-512 followup.
2) Add transient KV cache upper bound guard to serving runtime so a single request can't allocate >X% of GPU RAM (owner: Maya). Short-term patch; long-term: smarter per-session accounting.
3) Adjust router policy to prefer pool utilization when retry_count >= 1 (owner: Leah). This would reduce retries to same hot node.
4) Add alert: p95 gen latency + >200ms sustained for 3m AND node OOM events >0 -> escalate to pagers (owner: Dylan). Put rule in ops/prometheus/rules.

Notes for incident write-up:
- Impact: increased token latency and dropped requests for ~40 minutes; ~1.1k requests impacted. No data exfiltration, no auth issues.
- Proposed next day postmortem scope: sequence length distribution, kernel scheduling logs, autoscaler thresholds, and router retry heuristics.

Loose thoughts / ideas:
- Could we use a small LRU on-RAM cache for the most-common prefixes to avoid expensive KV cache population for tiny prompts? Might help the ‘many small prompt’ case. (cheap experiment)
- Consider a low-cost fast-fail path: if KV cache population would push memory >70% allocate, early-fail with an explicit 429 + retry-backoff header. Would surface backpressure to clients instead of node OOM.

Followups I've added to tickets:
- INF-2789: incident stub + raw logs attached (will tidy).
- SRE-512: autoscaler review checklist assigned to Chen.

Immediate manual TODO (my personal):
- 14:30 ping Chen on slack for autoscale thresholds.
- 15:00 draft short blurb for Ops channel summarizing mitigation and expected ETA for full fix.
- Before EOD: create small repro for KV cache spike (script + minimal client sim) and attach to INF-2789.

Random scratch:
- test script ideas: 200 concurrent clients sending 4–8 short prompts (seq len 60–120) with 50ms wait between. Measure kv-cache miss rate and mem usage.
- metrics to capture next run: per-session kv-alloc, kernel wait time, per-shard queue depth, router retry destinations.

End notes: keep this doc ephemeral. If anything becomes formalized (postmortem/PR), move to shared_drives/engineering/observability/incidents/INF-2789. For now, rough timeline + single-line ownership is enough to keep momentum.

-- Dylan
